repo_notes.content: pydomain is a Python 3.12+ library (dependencies: pydantic>=2.12.5, uuid-utils>=0.10, anyio>=4) for DDD, CQRS, event sourcing and sagas, adopted in five levels (README.md, 'The Five Adoption Levels'). The repository docs are the source of truth: ADRs in docs/adr/ (index docs/adr/README.md), the arc42 architecture in docs/arch42/, and the Diataxis user docs in docs/diataxis/ (getting-started, concepts, how-to, api-reference). When a page states a design decision, cite the ADR by number and link it. Do not state a fixed ADR count; the index grows with every fix.

Public names come from each package's __all__ (src/pydomain/__init__.py and the ddd, cqrs, cqrs.saga, es, infrastructure, testing and testing.contracts packages). Document only names that are exported there. Names that no longer exist and must not appear: FakeProcessedCommandStore and ProcessedCommandStore (now FakeProcessedMessageStore and ProcessedMessageStore), DistributedLockingBehavior (now AggregateLockingBehavior). Subscription and SubscriptionRunner live in pydomain.infrastructure, not pydomain.es.

Library errors, logs and reprs never carry payload values; they describe a value by type or field name only (ADR-071, src/pydomain/_describe.py). Examples on the wiki should follow the same rule and use clearly synthetic data such as orders and invoices.

Development uses GitFlow: branches fix|feature|chore|docs/DCE-NN-slug from dev, squash-merged by PR, with YouTrack issue keys DCE-NN in PR titles and code commits (checked by .github/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh). The bug-fix workflow is test-first with a strict-xfail red commit, mutation testing (make mutate MODULE=...) and two reviews (ADR-066). Release steps: docs/others/commit_and_release_guide.md.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to pydomain: what it is, why it exists, the five adoption levels (DDD; + CQRS; + MessageBus and UnitOfWork; + event sourcing; + snapshots, upcasting and subscriptions), and the layered module architecture. Links to all major sections.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Installation, requirements (Python 3.12+, pydantic>=2.12.5, uuid-utils>=0.10, anyio>=4), the dev extras and make targets (install, test, lint, type, check, mutate), and a quickstart that follows docs/diataxis/getting-started through the adoption levels.

pages.title: Architecture and Module Boundaries
pages.purpose: The layered dependency graph (ddd at the core; cqrs and es on top of it; infrastructure wiring them; testing providing fakes), the import rules enforced by pytest-archon in tests/test_architecture.py, the package exports checked by tests/test_package_exports.py, and how each module maps to an adoption level. Draws on docs/arch42/05-building-block-view.md.

pages.title: Domain Layer (pydomain.ddd)
pages.purpose: Overview of the tactical DDD primitives in pydomain.ddd, the innermost layer with no infrastructure dependencies, and its exceptions (DomainError, ConcurrencyError, SpecificationError). Links to the child pages.

pages.title: Entities, Value Objects, and Aggregate Roots
pages.purpose: Entity[TId], ValueObject and AggregateRoot[TId] as Pydantic v2 base classes: identity semantics and accepted ID types, value-object immutability, the pending-events buffer and pull_events(), and optimistic concurrency through the version field.

pages.title: Domain Events
pages.purpose: DomainEvent as a frozen Pydantic model: event_id, occurred_at, event_version, correlation_id and causation_id; stamp() returning a copy with the tracing IDs set; and publishing events only after the unit of work commits.

pages.title: Repository, Factory, Specification, and Domain Services
pages.purpose: The Repository[T, TId] protocol (save with an optional command_id, get_by_id, delete, pull_events); Factory[T] versus ReconstitutionFactory[T]; the DomainService marker; the Specification pattern with and_/or_/not_ (AndSpecification, OrSpecification, NotSpecification) and its serialization limits; and IdGenerator with Uuid7Generator.

pages.title: CQRS Layer (pydomain.cqrs)
pages.purpose: Overview of the CQRS module: commands and queries, the buses, pipeline behaviors, the unit of work, the transactional outbox, projections and integration events, and its exceptions (CQRSError, CommandExecutionError, NoHandlerRegisteredError, HandlerAlreadyRegisteredError, UnitOfWorkAlreadyCommittedError). Links to the child pages.

pages.title: Commands, Queries, and Buses
pages.purpose: Command[TResult] and Query[TResult] frozen models; CommandResult, QueryResult and EmptyCommandResult; CommandBus, QueryBus and EventBus registration and dispatch; the handler protocols (CommandHandler, QueryHandler, EventHandler); and fail-loud command handling versus isolated event-handler failures.

pages.title: Pipeline Behaviors and Middleware
pages.purpose: The MessagePipeline onion, the PipelineBehavior and NextHandler protocols, MessageContext and MessageKind, and the five built-in behaviors: LoggingBehavior, ValidationBehavior, IdempotencyBehavior and EventIdempotencyBehavior (ProcessedMessageStore, the MISSING sentinel, IdempotentCommandIgnored), and AggregateLockingBehavior (LockProvider, LockKeyResolver, DictLockKeyResolver, ordered keys to avoid deadlock).

pages.title: Unit of Work
pages.purpose: The UnitOfWork protocol and AbstractUnitOfWork: async context-manager lifecycle; commit() and rollback() and the overridable _flush, _commit and _rollback hooks; event collection and stamping with correlation and causation IDs; draining staged events on rollback; and the error raised on a second commit().

pages.title: Transactional Outbox
pages.purpose: Writing integration events in the same transaction as the aggregate: OutboxWriter passed to AbstractUnitOfWork, OutboundEventRegistry mapping domain events to integration events, OutboxEntry and the OutboxStore protocol, and the OutboundEventGateway relay (run_once, run, start, stop) that publishes pending entries to a MessageBroker.

pages.title: Projections and Integration Events
pages.purpose: The CQRS Projection[StateT] protocol (a left fold with apply and rebuild), the ProjectionStore protocol, and IntegrationEvent (primitives only, with string event_id and occurred_at for transport).

pages.title: Saga Subsystem (pydomain.cqrs.saga)
pages.purpose: Overview of saga orchestration for long-running processes: the on() DSL, SagaState, SagaManager, SagaRegistry, SagaRepository, compensation, and the saga exceptions (SagaError, SagaConfigurationError, SagaHandlerNotFoundError, SagaStateError). Links to the child pages.

pages.title: Saga Definition and Lifecycle
pages.purpose: The Saga[S] base class and the on() DSL mapping events to commands with optional compensation; the SagaStatus values (PENDING, RUNNING, SUSPENDED, COMPLETED, FAILED, COMPENSATING, COMPENSATED) and the allowed transitions between them; the SagaManager load-handle-save-dispatch cycle; SagaRegistry binding; hydrate_command; and the SagaRepository protocol.

pages.title: Saga State, Compensation, and Advanced Features
pages.purpose: SagaState fields (StepRecord step history, processed event IDs, the CompensationRecord stack, pending commands, suspension and timeout); LIFO compensation; idempotency through processed event IDs; suspension, resume and timeout; crash recovery; SagaPruningPolicy and StepThresholdPruningPolicy; and memory bounds.

pages.title: Event Sourcing Layer (pydomain.es)
pages.purpose: Overview of the event-sourcing module: EventSourcedAggregateRoot, EventStore, EventStream, EventSourcedRepository, snapshots, upcasting, event-sourced projections and checkpoints, and its exceptions (StreamNotFoundError, DuplicateCommandError, StaleSnapshotError, UpcastError). Links to the child pages.

pages.title: EventSourcedAggregateRoot and EventStore
pages.purpose: EventSourcedAggregateRoot[TId]: _apply, _when and _replay, version tracking and _snapshot_schema_version. The EventStore protocol (append_to_stream with an expected version and an optional command_id, read_stream, read_all), the EventStream value object, EventSourcedRepository, and command idempotency through DuplicateCommandError.

pages.title: Snapshots and Schema Versioning
pages.purpose: The Snapshot value object, the SnapshotStore protocol, SnapshotPolicy and SnapshotThresholdPolicy, SnapshotSchemaPolicy and RejectStaleSnapshotPolicy, StaleSnapshotError, snapshot-first hydration in EventSourcedRepository, and evolving _snapshot_schema_version.

pages.title: Event Upcasting and Schema Migration
pages.purpose: EventUpcaster (source_type, source_version, target_version, upcast()), UpcasterRegistry chain resolution and cycle detection, UpcastError, upcasting exactly once while EventRegistry deserializes, and the event_version field on DomainEvent.

pages.title: Event-Sourced Projections and Checkpoints
pages.purpose: EventSourcedProjection (convention-based _when_<EventName> dispatch, name and version class variables, checkpoint tracking) and the CheckpointStore protocol, and how SubscriptionRunner feeds projections from the event store.

pages.title: Infrastructure Layer (pydomain.infrastructure)
pages.purpose: Overview of the wiring layer: the MessageBus facade, bootstrap() and Application, EventRegistry, the MessageBroker and MessageSubscriber protocols, the outbound and inbound event gateways, and subscriptions. Links to the child pages.

pages.title: MessageBus and Application Bootstrap
pages.purpose: The MessageBus facade (one dispatch for Command, Query and DomainEvent; register_command, register_query, register_event; sequential event processing with isolated handler failures). The bootstrap() composition root: checking that each inbound gateway uses the application's bus, rejecting duplicate gateways, starting gateways and cleaning up after a partial start, and the Application lifecycle (dispatch, the component properties, shutdown order).

pages.title: EventRegistry and Event Serialization
pages.purpose: EventRegistry: register, serialize and deserialize; GenericDomainEvent as the fallback for unknown types; reading the stored event version; and UpcasterRegistry integration.

pages.title: Message Brokers, Gateways, and Subscriptions
pages.purpose: The MessageBroker protocol (publish, start, stop) and OutboundEventGateway; the MessageSubscriber protocol (subscribe, start, stop) and the InboundEventGateway anti-corruption layer (register_translation, acknowledging poison messages); and Subscription with SubscriptionRunner (polling, at-least-once delivery, failure backoff).

pages.title: Testing Infrastructure (pydomain.testing)
pages.purpose: Overview of pydomain.testing: in-memory fakes for every port, so domain and application logic can be tested without real infrastructure, and contract suites that check real adapters behave like the fakes (ADR-067). Links to the child pages.

pages.title: Fakes and In-Memory Test Doubles
pages.purpose: FakeRepository, FakeUnitOfWork, FakeLockProvider, FakeProcessedMessageStore, FakeOutboxStore, FakeSagaRepository, InMemoryProjectionStore, FakeEventStore (concurrency and duplicate-command checks, the global log), FakeSnapshotStore, FakeCheckpointStore, InMemoryMessageBroker and InMemoryMessageSubscriber, and how to wire them into a test suite with anyio.

pages.title: Contract Suites
pages.purpose: The reusable contract test classes in pydomain.testing.contracts (RepositoryContract, UnitOfWorkContract, EventStoreContract, SnapshotStoreContract, CheckpointStoreContract, OutboxStoreContract, ProcessedMessageStoreContract, LockProviderContract, MessageBrokerContract, MessageSubscriberContract, ProjectionStoreContract, SagaRepositoryContract): subclassing one with a fixture for your adapter, the hook methods, and the pinned async backend (ADR-067).

pages.title: Developer Workflow and Tooling
pages.purpose: The make targets, the pre-commit pipeline (ruff, mypy strict, check-commit-msg.sh), the GitHub Actions workflows (test.yml across Python 3.12 to 3.14, lint-commits.yml, block-breaking.yml, publish.yml), CODEOWNERS, mutation testing with mutmut, the runnable-docs test runner in tests/docs, GitFlow with DCE issue keys, and the test-first fix workflow (ADR-066).

pages.title: Architecture Decision Records and Documentation
pages.purpose: A guide to the ADRs in docs/adr/, grouped by module as in docs/adr/README.md (foundations, DDD, CQRS, sagas, event sourcing, infrastructure, process), and to the arc42 chapters in docs/arch42/ and the Diataxis docs in docs/diataxis/. Summarizes the key decisions: protocols versus ABCs, Pydantic v2, async-only APIs, the exception hierarchy, identity semantics, the unit of work and outbox, saga design, event sourcing, and keeping payload values out of errors and logs.
